body: This should return a `Vector<Point2i>`.

`selection_drag_attempt` is never set to `true` for touch input, this shouldn't be needed.
It looks like there is no selection drag and drop for touch, which is probably for the best.

Shouldn't the drag position be offset by where the touch was relative to the selection handles start/end pos when dragging started? Or at least to the center of the drag handle.
Since you are dragging the circle part of the handle.
Redraw should not be needed, `select` handles it.

Inertial scrolling is also relevant for mouse wheel scrolling and pan gesture scrolling, see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5386 https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13682
I haven't checked if this implementation is good for those other use cases, but maybe this could be applied for them as well.
This would be easier to test if it was added for those, but it could also be done in a different PR.

Does this work? `_update_selection_mode_pointer` is intended to be called on press, not on release.

With `p_initial` set and no selection, the only thing it really does is calls `adjust_viewport_to_caret`, which could be called here instead.
When it sets the selection origin and the word begin/end it is for later dragging or shift selecting, which doesn't apply. And it would try to start `click_select_held`, only for it to immediately be stopped in the `if (touch->is_released()) {` branch below.

(`_update_selection_mode_word` looks fine).
This variable is functionally unused, can be removed.

I think for `start_rect` in particular it should use `selection_from_column > 0 ? selection_from_column + 1 : 0` as the column instead of adding the rect size to it, because if the start is the first character on a wrapped line it would be in the wrong place. This way it is at the start of the next character instead.
`end_rect` is good as is, since it wants to be at the end of the character.
(yeah `get_rect_at_line_column` is pretty confusing, I'm working on a PR that should improve it).
These should check to make sure `start/end_pos.x != -1`
I wanted to add support for selection drag, just didn't figured out an action to trigger it. But I think, I'll just remove this for now and do in a seperate follow-up.

And, yeah other control nodes should be handled in seperate PR.
This was copied from the mouse handling logic, and yeah, It's just adjusting viewport here. I agree, it's probably best to just call `adjust_viewport_to_caret`.

Does it work at the start of a wrapped line? The from column won't be 0 so the pos will be at the end of the rect, but it will use the rect from the previous character which would be on the previous wrap.

Ok, I can reproduce the issue with wrapped line. > `end_rect` is good as is, since it wants to be at the end of the character. No, there's also issue with this. The end handle should be at the caret position there:

> I think for `start_rect` in particular it should use `selection_from_column > 0 ? selection_from_column + 1 : 0` as the column instead of adding the rect size to it, because if the start is the first character on a wrapped line it would be in the wrong place. This way it is at the start of the next character instead. `get_rect_at_line_column` would throw error when handle is at the end of the line Because, we would be increasing the column by one everytime.

Fixed!

Since the issue was caused by wrapped lines. My fix checks whether the selection from/to column is the first column in a wrapped line segment. If it is, the rect size is not added, preventing the extra offset.

These lines can be removed, its not starting a selection.

I've noticed this feels a little off. 
The `selection_handle_drag_offset` is set relative to the start/end pos, which is at the very top of the line, which means if you move your finger up even slightly then the selection will go to the previous line.
Instead the corrected text pos should be at the center of the line when it hasn't moved yet.

So it should be:
```suggestion
			Vector2 corrected_text_pos = drag->get_position() - selection_handle_drag_offset + Vector2(0, get_line_height() / 2.0);
```
 (or could be part of offset)

`TextEdit::_update_minimap_click` checks minimap bounds, it is needed for double tap too.
Currently double tapping on the minimap tries to select the closest word, when it should operate the minimap.

It's currently not fixed for touch. If you pan with two fingers and then lift them, the caret is immediately repositioned, which isn't the desired behavior.

This PR isn't addressing that issue because I'd like to keep panning disabled. I don't see any use case for it.

I had initially kept the drag offset from the center of the line, but after testing, I felt that using the top position worked better actually. I'll test it a few more times, but so far I prefer the offset from the top.

Edit: Updated offset. However, I'm still not sure about this one...

What if someone tries the gesture? It won't work as they expect it to. 
Even though there is a new way to scroll now, users are still going to try it. Especially if they are used to the previous behavior when it at least scrolled. I don't see why it should be disallowed.

Before this PR, I didn't even know that was possible. I don't think there's much chance anyone was using it because, before this PR, panning also selected the text, just like dragging with a single finger.

I guess, I found a use case, pan gesture is good for speed scrooll. But... we already have scrollbars for that :P

Edit:

> It's currently not fixed for touch. If you pan with two fingers and then lift them, the caret is immediately repositioned, which isn't the desired behavior.

OK, fixed the virtual keyboard popup issue and re-enabled panning.

I feel that currently with the half-line offset it feels better, particularly because the distance to get to the next and previous lines are the same from the starting position. 
Was the top offset better to you because it had a greater distance from the touch position in general? In that case we could move the handle down or make the handle radius bigger, or even just increase the radius for touching it but not visually.

Should we adjust to caret here? This way dragging a handle to the edge will scroll so you can keep selecting in that direction, like mouse selecting does. But IDK if the screen space is too small it could maybe cause unwanted scrolling. And I'm not sure if it will work with the offset.

Can't really say why I preferred the top offset, it just felt a bit better to me. That said, I don't think the centered position is much of an issue either.

Let's go with the current implementation for now and revisit it later when we get some community feedback.

Yes, that might work. However, I'll send a follow-up PR for this togther with some other selection handle enhancements.

I don't want to take risk in this PR at this point :P

Edit: tested it. It works, but as expected there are some issues. For instance, it only works when dragging the caret handle.
Can you turn `10.0` into a constant, and add a comment to explain why that value was selected.

The value was chosen after trying a few different radii. `10.0` provided the best balance between being easy to grab without making the touch area feel too large. I plan to iterate on it after community testing and feedback.

As for turning it into a constant, I don't think it's necessary since it's only used in this one place. We also use literals directly in similar cases elsewhere.

> The value was chosen after trying a few different radii. 10.0 provided the best balance between being easy to grab without making the touch area feel too large. I plan to iterate on it after community testing and feedback.

Added this as a comment there.
